summary: whalibmob 5.33.21: static keyword co-occurrences without traced installer-harm behavior
details: Package ships JavaScript files that import fs/http/https and reference tokens such as 'ping', 'curl', and 'hostname' alongside network primitives (lib/MediaService.js uses fs.readFileSync and https.request; lib/WebVersion.js references curl and https.get; lib/Registration.js and lib/socks.js contain 'ping'/'curl'/'POST' tokens). These are keyword co-occurrences in the shipped sources and do not, on their own, demonstrate reading of installer-owned secrets (no traced reads of ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, browser or wallet stores, or whole-environment dumps), do not name a non-first-party destination receiving installer data, and are not shown to execute at install, require, or import time via a lifecycle hook or top-level side effect. No hardcoded attacker C2, obfuscated destination, dropper, backdoor listener, or credential-harvesting pattern is identifiable from the available evidence.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
